hypothesis: The NullPointerException occurs because the code attempts to call .toString().length() on an object in the array when that object's toString() method returns null. This happens during the initial capacity calculation for the StringBuilder in the join method.
prediction: The code at line 3298 and 3383 will throw a NullPointerException if array[startIndex].toString() returns null, because the result of the ternary operator is used to call .length().
experiment_rationale: The stack trace and code snippets clearly show the NPE occurring at the StringBuilder initialization line where .toString().length() is invoked. The bug report confirms this behavior.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an incorrect algorithmic approach to estimating the initial capacity of a StringBuilder. Instead of relying on the actual content of the objects (which might return null from toString()), the implementation should use a safe default capacity or a different estimation strategy. This is a procedural/algorithmic error in how the buffer is initialized.
